summary.model: gemini-3.8-flash AFTER rollback checks: regression (rollback faults)

report.summary: Frontend checkout failed with HTTP 502 because the orders service returned HTTP 500 on POST /orders. Newly deployed revision orders-00002 introduced Decimal objects in order totals, which raised an unhandled TypeError during json.dumps in serialize_order_v2. Reverting orders to orders-00001 resolves the issue.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision orders-00002 introduced commit 9f3c2ab ('refactor(orders): keep totals as Decimal, add bulk discount line'). Python standard library json.dumps cannot serialize Decimal objects, causing TypeError: Object of type Decimal is not JSON serializable in serialize_order_v2 when validating the response payload. The previous revision orders-00001 had zero 5xx errors, and errors began immediately upon deployment of orders-00002.

report.summary: Payments revision payments-00002 removed the PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL environment variable, causing an unhandled KeyError: 'PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL' in payments.py load_gateway_config during POST /charge. This resulted in HTTP 500 errors from payments, which cascaded as HTTP 502 errors to orders and frontend checkout. Rollback to payments-00001 restores the missing environment variable and resolves the issue.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision payments-00002 removed the environment variable PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL, but payments.py load_gateway_config still accesses env['PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL'], throwing KeyError on every POST /charge. payments-00001 had zero errors, and all errors began immediately upon payments-00002 going live.

report.summary: Checkout requests failed with 502/503 errors due to database connection pool exhaustion in the orders service. Revision orders-00002 reduced DB_POOL_SIZE from 10 to 1, causing SQLAlchemy QueuePool limit timeout errors as soon as multiple requests ran concurrently. Rolling back orders to orders-00001 restores the pool capacity to 10 connections.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision orders-00002 changed DB_POOL_SIZE from 10 to 1, causing QueuePool connection timeouts under concurrent checkout requests. Errors appeared immediately after orders-00002 was deployed and did not occur on orders-00001.

report.summary: Frontend began failing requests with 503 status codes due to container instances being terminated with OOMKilled (exit code 137). Revision frontend-00002 configured PRODUCT_CACHE to 'unbounded', causing memory usage to exceed the 512 MiB container limit. Logs confirm memory reaching 530 MiB (104% of limit) followed by instance termination and 503 responses on GET /products.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision frontend-00002 changed PRODUCT_CACHE from 'lru:256' to 'unbounded' in commit 5b6a1f4 ('perf(frontend): cache product catalogue responses'). This unbounded in-memory cache caused container memory usage to exceed the 512 MiB limit (reaching 530 MiB), leading to Cloud Run OOMKilled container termination (exit code 137) and 503 errors on GET /products. Previous revision frontend-00001 had stable memory usage (~140 MiB) and zero 5xx errors.

report.summary: Deployment of revision orders-00002 introduced a code change storing totals as Decimal objects, which cannot be serialized by standard json.dumps in serialize_order_v2. This raises an unhandled TypeError on POST /orders, resulting in 500 errors to frontend and 502 Bad Gateway responses to clients on POST /checkout. Log evidence shows all errors isolated to orders-00002 starting immediately after its release.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision orders-00002 introduced commit 9f3c2ab ('refactor(orders): keep totals as Decimal, add bulk discount line'). In demo/serializers.py line 23 (serialize_order_v2), json.dumps(out) is called with an unhandled Decimal object, raising TypeError: Object of type Decimal is not JSON serializable and resulting in HTTP 500 responses. Errors started immediately with orders-00002 deployment and never occurred on orders-00001.

report.summary: Revision payments-00002 removed the required PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL environment variable, causing POST /charge in the payments service to fail immediately with an unhandled KeyError. This led to cascading 502 errors upstream in orders and frontend checkout. Log entries confirm payments-00002 throwing KeyError on PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL starting right after its deployment.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision payments-00002 removed the environment variable PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL ('https://gateway.example.com/v2 -> (removed)'). When handling POST /charge, load_gateway_config attempts to read env['PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL'], raising KeyError and causing HTTP 500 errors in payments and cascading 502 errors to orders and frontend. Prior revision payments-00001 had zero errors and had the variable configured.

report.summary: Deploying orders-00002 reduced DB_POOL_SIZE from 10 to 1, causing immediate database connection pool exhaustion and SQLAlchemy QueuePool timeouts under traffic. The orders service returned HTTP 503, which caused frontend POST /checkout requests to fail with HTTP 502. Prior revision orders-00001 had a pool size of 10 and 0% error rate.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision orders-00002 updated DB_POOL_SIZE from 10 to 1, causing SQLAlchemy QueuePool connection exhaustion and timeouts on concurrent requests. No errors occurred on orders-00001, which had DB_POOL_SIZE=10.

report.summary: Frontend revision frontend-00002 configured an unbounded product cache via env var PRODUCT_CACHE ('lru:256 -> unbounded'), causing memory usage to exceed the 512 MiB limit (reaching 549 MiB). Cloud Run OOM-killed the container instance (exit code 137), leading to 503 errors on incoming GET /products requests. Logs and metrics show frontend-00001 was healthy (~140 MiB memory, 0 errors, 0 restarts) until frontend-00002 was deployed.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision frontend-00002 changed PRODUCT_CACHE from 'lru:256' to 'unbounded' alongside commit 5b6a1f4 ('perf(frontend): cache product catalogue responses'), which caused frontend memory usage to surge past the 512 MiB container limit to 549 MiB. The container was repeatedly OOMKilled (exit code 137), producing 503 errors on GET /products; previous revision frontend-00001 had zero 5xx errors and stable memory (~140 MiB).

report.summary: Deployment of revision orders-00002 broke order serialization by introducing Decimal objects that standard json.dumps cannot serialize, throwing unhandled TypeErrors. This caused POST /orders to return HTTP 500, leading to frontend checkout failures (HTTP 502). Log evidence confirms failures began immediately upon deploying orders-00002 and do not occur on orders-00001.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision orders-00002 deployed commit '9f3c2ab refactor(orders): keep totals as Decimal, add bulk discount line' at 2026-10-02T20:56:06.338Z. Immediately at 2026-10-02T20:56:06.377Z, POST /orders started failing with 'TypeError: Object of type Decimal is not JSON serializable' during json.dumps in serialize_order_v2. No errors occurred on orders-00001, and frontend errors (HTTP 502) are directly downstream of orders 500 responses.

report.summary: Deployment of revision payments-00002 removed the PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL environment variable while the service code still required it. This caused POST /charge to crash with KeyError: 'PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL' on every request, cascading 500 errors to orders and 502 errors to frontend checkout.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision payments-00002 removed PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL ('https://gateway.example.com/v2 -> (removed)'), causing load_gateway_config to fail with KeyError: 'PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL' on all POST /charge requests. The previous revision payments-00001 had a 0% error rate and contained this required configuration.

report.summary: The orders service failed with QueuePool connection timeouts after revision orders-00002 reduced DB_POOL_SIZE from 10 to 1. This caused orders to return HTTP 503 on POST /orders, leading to HTTP 502 failures on frontend POST /checkout. Metrics and logs confirm the failure started immediately upon the deployment of orders-00002 with db_pool_in_use pegged at capacity.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision orders-00002 deployed commit c81e5d0 which reduced DB_POOL_SIZE from 10 to 1. Under concurrent load, the single database connection was exhausted immediately, causing QueuePool timeout errors and HTTP 503 responses that cascaded to frontend as HTTP 502s. Previous revision orders-00001 had zero 5xx errors.

report.summary: The frontend service began returning 503 errors on GET /products due to container instances being OOM-killed (exit code 137). Revision frontend-00002 enabled unbounded caching of product catalogue responses via PRODUCT_CACHE="unbounded", causing memory usage to exceed the 512 MiB limit (reaching 589 MiB). Rolling back to frontend-00001 restores the bounded LRU cache and stabilizes memory.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision frontend-00002 introduced commit 5b6a1f4 ('perf(frontend): cache product catalogue responses') and changed PRODUCT_CACHE from 'lru:256' to 'unbounded'. This unbounded in-memory cache caused container memory to surge past the 512 MiB limit (reaching 589 MiB), resulting in exit code 137 (OOMKilled) container terminations and HTTP 503 errors on GET /products. Previous revision frontend-00001 had zero restarts, steady 140 MiB memory usage, and zero 5xx errors.

report.summary: The frontend POST /checkout endpoint is returning HTTP 502 because the upstream orders service is failing with HTTP 500 on POST /orders. Newly deployed revision orders-00002 introduced commit 9f3c2ab storing totals as Decimal, which crashes serialize_order_v2 with an unhandled TypeError as Decimal is not JSON serializable. The errors started immediately when orders-00002 went live and do not occur on orders-00001.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision orders-00002 introduced commit '9f3c2ab refactor(orders): keep totals as Decimal, add bulk discount line'. The standard json.dumps() in serialize_order_v2 raises 'TypeError: Object of type Decimal is not JSON serializable' when serializing Decimal values, causing HTTP 500 errors on POST /orders and upstream HTTP 502 errors on frontend POST /checkout. Previous revision orders-00001 had zero 5xx errors and all exceptions are isolated to orders-00002.

report.summary: Frontend checkout requests are failing with HTTP 502 because the payments service is failing all POST /charge requests with HTTP 500 due to an unhandled KeyError: 'PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL'. Revision payments-00002 removed the PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL environment variable while the code still accesses it directly. Prior revision payments-00001 served traffic with zero errors, and rolling back payments to payments-00001 will restore the missing configuration.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision payments-00002 removed environment variable PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL ('https://gateway.example.com/v2 -> (removed)'), but payments.py load_gateway_config directly reads env['PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL']. This caused all POST /charge requests on payments-00002 to fail with KeyError: 'PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL', cascading 500 errors to orders and 502 errors to frontend. The previous revision payments-00001 had zero errors.

report.summary: Frontend POST /checkout failed with 5xx because the downstream orders service exhausted its database connection pool and returned HTTP 503. Revision orders-00002 changed DB_POOL_SIZE from 10 to 1, causing SQLAlchemy QueuePool timeouts under concurrent load. Logs and metrics show db_pool_in_use pinned at 1 and QueuePool TimeoutErrors appearing only on orders-00002.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision orders-00002 reduced DB_POOL_SIZE from 10 to 1 (commit c81e5d0). This shrank the database connection pool so that any concurrent request immediately caused QueuePool limit of size 1 overflow 0 timeouts on orders, bubbling up as HTTP 503 to frontend. Prior revision orders-00001 had a 0% error rate with DB_POOL_SIZE=10, and errors only appeared once orders-00002 began serving.

report.summary: Revision frontend-00002 configured PRODUCT_CACHE to 'unbounded', causing frontend memory usage to rapidly exceed the 512 MiB container limit on GET /products requests. The container was OOM-killed (exit code 137), producing HTTP 503 errors during restarts. Prior revision frontend-00001 had stable memory usage around 140 MiB with zero restarts or errors.
report.rollback_evidence: Revision frontend-00002 changed PRODUCT_CACHE from 'lru:256' to 'unbounded' along with commit '5b6a1f4 perf(frontend): cache product catalogue responses'. This unbounded caching caused memory to surge from ~140 MiB to 587 MiB within seconds, exceeding the 512 MiB limit and causing Cloud Run to terminate the container (exit code 137, OOMKilled), leading to 503 errors on GET /products. Reverting to frontend-00001 restores bounded caching and resolves the issue.
